pl-l4d5c1-d1e115.summary: States that the sacrament of baptism is given by good and bad ministers, as it is received by good and bad. Baptism is not better when given by a better minister, nor worse when given by a lesser or bad one; the gift is equal, since it is not man's but God's.
claims: Baptism is given validly by good and bad ministers.
The gift of baptism is equal whoever gives it, since it is God's.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e118.summary: Announces that all this is shown by the following testimonies.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: baptism is such as he in whose power it is given, not such as he by whose ministry it is given.
claims: The quality of baptism depends on Christ's power, not the minister.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e131.summary: Adds Augustine: it is entirely possible that some have true baptism without true faith.
claims: True baptism can exist without true faith.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e137.summary: Adds Augustine: if among good ministers, one better than another, the baptism given by the better is not better, then baptism given by a bad minister is in no way bad, since the same baptism is given; God's gift is equal through unequal ministers, being his, not theirs.
claims: Baptism is equal regardless of the minister's goodness.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e143.summary: Adds Augustine: when a bad man baptizes, what is given is one and not unequal because of unequal ministers, but equal, because 'this is he who baptizes'.
claims: Christ is the one who baptizes, so baptism is equal.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e149.summary: Adds Augustine: ministers of so great a judge ought to be just; let them be just if they will, but if those who sit in Moses' seat will not be just, my master has made me secure, of whom the Spirit says 'this is he who baptizes'.
claims: Ministers ought to be just, but their injustice does not endanger baptism.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e155.summary: Adds Augustine: those whom Judas baptized, Christ baptized; so if a drunkard, murderer, or adulterer baptized with Christ's baptism, Christ baptized. I do not fear them, for I look to the dove, through whom I am told 'this is he who baptizes'.
claims: Christ baptizes even through unworthy ministers.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e161.summary: Adds Augustine: a murderer gave Christ's baptism, a sacrament so holy that it is not polluted even by a murderer ministering.
claims: The sacrament is not polluted by the minister's sin.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e168.summary: Adds Augustine: one baptized in any heresy or schism in the name of the Father, Son, and Spirit has received the whole sacrament, but not salvation, the sacrament's power, if he has it outside the Catholic Church. He must return to the Church, not to receive baptism again, which no one may repeat, but to receive life in Catholic communion, since baptism profits only where almsgiving profits, in the Church.
claims: Baptism in heresy with the Trinitarian form is a whole sacrament.
Baptism does not profit unto salvation outside the Church.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e174.summary: Quotes Isidore: the Roman Pontiff judges not the man who baptizes but that the Spirit of God ministers the grace of baptism, even if a pagan baptizes.
claims: Even a pagan can validly baptize.

pl-l4d5c1-d1e180.summary: Concludes that true baptism is given to good and bad by good and bad, and that it is equally holy and its gift equal in the good, whether baptized by good or bad ministers; the reason follows in the next chapter.
claims: Baptism is equally holy whoever gives it.

pl-l4d5c1.summary: Teaches that baptism is given by good and bad ministers, as it is received by good and bad, and is equally holy whoever gives it, since it is God's gift, not man's. A string of Augustinian texts makes the point: baptism is such as he in whose power it is given, not such as the minister; whom Judas baptized, Christ baptized; a murderer's baptism is not polluted; baptism received in heresy or schism with the Trinitarian form is the whole sacrament, but its saving power is had only within the Church, to which the person must return, not to be rebaptized but to receive life. Isidore adds that the Pope judges that the Spirit gives the grace of baptism even if a pagan baptizes. The conclusion continues into the next chapter.
claims: Baptism given by a bad minister is as true and holy as that given by a good one.
Baptism is God's gift, not the minister's.
Baptism received outside the Church is a true sacrament but does not profit unto salvation outside it.
